item.description:
Last authors: Gianluigi A. Botton, Patrick Fournier

Authors: Maxime Dion, Guo-zhen Zhu, Guillaume Hardy, Gianluigi A. Botton, Patrick Fournier

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of Mott insulating interface in cuprate heterostructures, strong correlation physics.

Tags: #experiment #cuprate #superconductivity #Mottinsulator #heterostructure #transport

Abstract: The p - n junction is at the heart of the first great technological revolution. Here, the authors fabricate and characterize such a junction made entirely out of cuprates superconductors thin films. They observe a charge transfer between n -type Pr 1 . 85 Ce 0 . 15 CuO 4 and p -type La 1 . 85 Sr 0 . 15 CuO 4 , from which a Mott insulating layer emerges at the atomically sharp interface. They first assess the quality of the structure through x-ray diffraction and scanning transmission electron microscopy and then they explore the nature of the insulating interface arising from strong electron correlations with various electrical transport experiments.

Abstract: Two-dimensional moiré materials feature widely tunable electronic structures. When these materials are illuminated by light, they exhibit optical gyrotropy in the form of circular dichroism and birefringence. Here, the authors show that this gyrotropy naturally decomposes into an intrinsic contribution due to interlayer electronic coupling and an extrinsic contribution due to the twisted embedding of the material in physical space. The authors conduct a general symmetry analysis applicable to moiré materials and identify regimes in which the intrinsic, and in which the extrinsic contributions dominate the gyrotropy. Finally, they apply the analysis to twisted bilayer graphene and twisted MoTe 2 .
